newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI revises interest on expat forex deposits.
newsitem.headline: India RBI revises interest on expat forex deposits.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Saturday it had increased interest on pound sterling deposits maintained under the foreign currency (Non-Resident) accounts (Banks) (FCNRB) scheme.
Effective November 18, 1996, interest on sterling deposits with maturity from six months to less than one year would be raised to 5.25 percent per annum from 4.75, the RBI said in a statement.
Interest on Deutsche Mark (DM) deposits would attract interest of 2.75 percent per annum against three percent for deposits of six months and above but less than a year.
RBI said there would be no change in the existing interest rates on sterling and DM deposits of other maturities.
The RBI also announced a reduction in the interest on deposits maintained in Japanese yen and US dollars by 25 basis points in all maturities from one year to three years.

Interest on yen deposits of six months and above but less than one year would be unchanged at 0.50 percent per annum, it said. Similarly, interest on dollar deposits of six months and above but less than one year would be unchanged at 4.5 percent.
